body: Finding: Slide Scout is defined as a small, read-only desktop browser for local OME-Zarr 0.5 bioimaging filesets, and the admitted brief sets the current product boundary at local filesystem reading. Source evidence: inputs/brief.md line 3 and line 5 (sha256 f4f88faef06f7cc95c6935e2e43afe562bbdfc29ee85d984f8c59f0232c8556a, 905 bytes, 5 lines; read in full with bounded read_file). Governing conditions: access is read-only; inputs are local files; the target format version is pinned to OME-Zarr 0.5. Qualifications: the brief does not define the term fileset, so the unit of navigation (one Zarr store versus a directory tree of several stores) is not fixed by the admitted text. Counterevidence: none is available inside the admitted corpus, because no corpus beyond the brief was readable; absence of counterevidence is not evidence of absence. Applicability and transfer limits: this scope statement binds Slide Scout v1 only and must not be transferred to editing, export, remote-service, or clinical products, which line 5 explicitly excludes. Plan implications: any thin plan must treat local-read-only as a hard architectural constraint (no write path is ever opened against source data). Unresolved: an authoritative definition and feature list of OME-Zarr 0.5 could not be verified against a specification copy in this workspace. Proposed validation (UNEXECUTED): read an admitted copy of the OME-Zarr 0.5 specification when one becomes available and confirm the scope wording against it.

Finding: the brief pins the supported format to OME-Zarr 0.5 and simultaneously requires the product to clearly explain data it cannot display, which together make explicit format-version detection and version-specific messaging a first-class requirement rather than an implementation detail. Source evidence: inputs/brief.md line 3 (sha256 f4f88faef06f7cc95c6935e2e43afe562bbdfc29ee85d984f8c59f0232c8556a). Governing conditions: version detection must happen before any decode attempt so that failure is explained rather than crashed. Qualifications and counterevidence: scientists will in practice hand over datasets written against other spec revisions (for example 0.4-era files); a hard refusal for anything not exactly 0.5 would conflict with the usability goal, so the policy for near versions is a product decision the brief leaves open. Applicability and transfer limits: knowledge of the exact feature differences between 0.4 and 0.5 is model knowledge and could not be checked against any specification document in the workspace; it must not be cited as corpus fact. Plan implications: implement version sniffing on open, a documented support matrix, and a distinct user-facing message class for unsupported or ambiguous versions. Unresolved: the definitive 0.5 feature delta and the minimum viable 0.4 fallback. Proposed validation (UNEXECUTED): build small fixture datasets conforming to 0.4 and 0.5 respectively and record actual open-time behavior of the chosen reader.

Finding: the brief requires that scientists can find images within a fileset, which implies collection enumeration, hierarchy browsing, and some search or filter capability as core navigation requirements. Source evidence: inputs/brief.md line 3 (sha256 f4f88faef06f7cc95c6935e2e43afe562bbdfc29ee85d984f8c59f0232c8556a). Governing conditions: navigation operates over local directory trees only. Qualifications: model knowledge (labeled as such, not corpus-verified) says OME-Zarr collections commonly use group hierarchies with plate and well metadata for screen-style data, plus standalone image groups; real filesets mix these shapes and may be inconsistent. Counterevidence: not every fileset is a plate; single-image folders are common, so the navigation layer must degrade to a simple list. Applicability and transfer limits: plate and well assumptions must not be applied to non-screen data. Plan implications: a scan or catalog layer that walks the local tree, identifies image groups, and exposes a searchable index is needed before any viewer work; scan must be lazy and interruptible because filesets can be large. Unresolved: the intended meaning and size range of a fileset, since the thin plan was not readable in this workspace. Proposed validation (UNEXECUTED): assemble fixture corpora covering a single image, a plate with wells and fields, and a nested ad-hoc tree, then exercise the scanner against all three.

Finding: the brief requires inspection of multiresolution images by channel, time point and plane, so dynamic axis handling and pyramid-level selection are core viewer requirements, not conveniences. Source evidence: inputs/brief.md line 3 (sha256 f4f88faef06f7cc95c6935e2e43afe562bbdfc29ee85d984f8c59f0232c8556a). Governing conditions: which axes exist is data-dependent; the UI must adapt to the axes actually declared rather than assume a fixed order. Qualifications: model knowledge (labeled, not corpus-verified) says OME-Zarr stores multiscale pyramids as successive dataset levels with declared axes and per-level coordinate transformations, and that single-resolution datasets without a pyramid also occur. Counterevidence: absent pyramid levels contradict a viewer that always assumes levels exist; missing time or channel axes contradict fixed four-dimensional UIs. Applicability and transfer limits: axis-count and ordering assumptions valid for one fileset do not transfer to another. Plan implications: the image model should be axes-driven, with level choice derived from viewport size and chunked, on-demand reads of only the requested channel, time point and plane. Unresolved: whether the thin plan prescribed specific level-selection heuristics, since the plan artifact was not readable. Proposed validation (UNEXECUTED): fixture set with 2D, 3D, 4D and 5D datasets, with and without pyramids, and assert correct slicing of every axis combination.

Finding: the brief requires overlay of associated label images, making label support a stated capability, but the qualifier associated signals that labels are optional per-dataset data rather than an always-present obligation. Source evidence: inputs/brief.md line 3 (sha256 f4f88faef06f7cc95c6935e2e43afe562bbdfc29ee85d984f8c59f0232c8556a). Governing conditions: overlay must degrade gracefully when no label image is associated. Qualifications: model knowledge (labeled, not corpus-verified) says OME-Zarr associates labels with an image through a sibling labels group and label-specific metadata including color tables; pixel geometry is expected to match the source image but this must be verified per file rather than trusted. Counterevidence: many bioimaging filesets contain no labels at all; some contain labels whose size or axis order disagrees with the base image, which is exactly the class of data the brief says must be explained when it cannot be displayed. Applicability and transfer limits: label conventions differ between spec revisions; conclusions drawn for 0.5 must not be silently applied to older files. Plan implications: the viewer needs an overlay toggle, per-label color mapping and opacity control, and an explicit mismatch diagnostic path. Unresolved: the exact 0.5 label metadata contract. Proposed validation (UNEXECUTED): fixtures with well-formed labels, absent labels, and mismatched label geometry, asserting the three distinct behaviors.

Finding: the brief requires correctly calibrated coordinates, which elevates axis units and coordinate transformations to correctness-critical data: a viewer that silently substitutes default units or scales will mislead scientists about physical sizes. Source evidence: inputs/brief.md line 3 (sha256 f4f88faef06f7cc95c6935e2e43afe562bbdfc29ee85d984f8c59f0232c8556a). Governing conditions: calibration must be derived from the file, and when units are absent the honest behavior is to mark them unknown, not to guess. Qualifications: model knowledge (labeled, not corpus-verified) says OME-Zarr declares axes with optional units and per-level scale and translation transformations, and that legacy files frequently omit units. Counterevidence: defaulting to micrometers is common in ecosystem tooling precisely because many files lack units, so there is ecosystem pressure toward the wrong behavior; the brief's wording argues against it. Applicability and transfer limits: unit conventions differ across axes types (time versus space); a single default is wrong by construction. Plan implications: scale bars, coordinate readouts and plane spacing must flow through a unit-aware layer with an explicit unknown-unit state surfaced in the UI. Unresolved: the complete transformation algebra defined by the 0.5 specification. Proposed validation (UNEXECUTED): fixture with known physical pixel size and known transforms, asserting displayed calibration matches ground truth, plus a unit-less fixture asserting the unknown state appears.

Finding: the brief requires that the product remain responsive while opening large saved datasets, a non-functional requirement that constrains the entire read path toward lazy, chunk-level access and away from whole-volume loads. Source evidence: inputs/brief.md line 3 (sha256 f4f88faef06f7cc95c6935e2e43afe562bbdfc29ee85d984f8c59f0232c8556a). Governing conditions: responsiveness is required during opening specifically, which points at scan, header read, and first-frame paths. Qualifications: the brief states no numeric budget, so any concrete target (for example first image visible in under two seconds on a multi-gigabyte fileset) is a proposed product decision, not a corpus fact. Counterevidence: model knowledge (labeled, not corpus-verified) suggests naive readers that decompress whole planes or whole volumes exist in the ecosystem, so this requirement genuinely discriminates between reader implementations. Applicability and transfer limits: measured results on one filesystem or chunking layout do not transfer to others. Plan implications: define a performance budget, select a reader with chunk-aligned partial reads and background decoding, and instrument open latency. Unresolved: real-world size distribution of target datasets. Proposed validation (UNEXECUTED): benchmark open-to-first-image latency on a multi-gigabyte fixture before and after reader choice, results to be recorded in a later observation version.

Finding: the brief requires the product to clearly explain data it cannot display, which implies an error and diagnostic taxonomy covering at least unsupported format versions, missing or invalid metadata, unreadable or corrupt chunks, and unsupported encodings, with per-image rather than per-session granularity. Source evidence: inputs/brief.md line 3 (sha256 f4f88faef06f7cc95c6935e2e43afe562bbdfc29ee85d984f8c59f0232c8556a). Governing conditions: explanations must be actionable and must not block the rest of a fileset from being browsed. Qualifications: the brief does not enumerate failure modes; the taxonomy above is analysis, and model knowledge (labeled, not corpus-verified) indicates failures are usually partial, for example one broken pyramid level or an unreadable compressor while other levels are fine. Counterevidence: a design that hides partial failures behind a blank tile would technically display but would not explain, contradicting the brief. Applicability and transfer limits: failure modes specific to remote storage do not apply within the local-only boundary. Plan implications: the reader layer should return structured, classified errors instead of exceptions escaping to the UI, and the UI should render per-image diagnostic states with reasons. Unresolved: the full space of 0.5 validation failures documented by the spec. Proposed validation (UNEXECUTED): fault-injection fixtures (truncated chunk, missing .zattrs-equivalent metadata, unknown compressor) asserting each produces a distinct, human-readable explanation.

Finding: the brief states that source files must remain unchanged, an integrity invariant that binds every layer: file handles must be opened read-only, no locks, no write-through caches, and no metadata sidecar files may be created inside or beside source trees. Source evidence: inputs/brief.md line 5 (sha256 f4f88faef06f7cc95c6935e2e43afe562bbdfc29ee85d984f8c59f0232c8556a). Governing conditions: this is an absolute constraint on the current product boundary, not a default. Qualifications and counterevidence: model knowledge (labeled, not corpus-verified) indicates some Zarr ecosystem tooling writes consolidated metadata files into source trees as an optimization and some libraries create caches or lock files implicitly; if the chosen reader does any of this, it is disqualifying or requires a wrapper, because the invariant is absolute. Applicability and transfer limits: none; this condition applies to every feature including search indexing and thumbnail generation, which must cache outside source trees. Plan implications: any thumbnail or scan cache must live in an application-owned directory; integrity must be testable, so the plan needs a checksum harness. Unresolved: whether any admitted corpus source discusses permitted in-place optimizations; none was readable. Proposed validation (UNEXECUTED): automated test that hashes an entire fixture tree, opens and fully browses it through the product, re-hashes, and asserts byte equality.

Finding: the brief explicitly excludes image editing, export, remote services and clinical interpretation from the current case, and sets the product boundary at local filesystem reading. Source evidence: inputs/brief.md line 5 (sha256 f4f88faef06f7cc95c6935e2e43afe562bbdfc29ee85d984f8c59f0232c8556a). Governing conditions: these exclusions define v1 scope; the brief does not claim they are permanent product limits. Qualifications: exclusions have interaction consequences, for example remote URLs will appear in drag-and-drop or open-dialog flows and must be rejected with a clear message consistent with R008, rather than failing obscurely. Counterevidence: none within the admitted corpus. Applicability and transfer limits: this observation must be revisited if the product boundary moves; nothing here may be cited as a claim about remote-capable architectures. Plan implications: no export or edit affordances in the UI; input validation limited to local paths; no clinical language anywhere in the interface; every exclusion should surface as a designed message state rather than silent absence. Unresolved: none material. Proposed validation (UNEXECUTED): interaction test asserting a remote URL input produces the designed local-only explanation message.

Finding: the brief itself demands a distinction between established format obligations and optional capabilities or choices that need a product decision, so the research output must carry that classification rather than a flat requirement list. Source evidence: inputs/brief.md line 5 (sha256 f4f88faef06f7cc95c6935e2e43afe562bbdfc29ee85d984f8c59f0232c8556a). Classification produced (format-obligation items labeled as model knowledge pending spec verification, since no specification document was readable in this workspace): obligations include interpreting multiscale level structure, declared axes and units, coordinate transformations, associated label conventions, and plate, well and field metadata where present; product decisions include default pyramid level and rendering defaults when metadata is absent, search interface shape, performance budgets, policy toward near-version files such as 0.4, and the depth of diagnostics. Qualifications and counterevidence: the obligation side is exactly where unverifiable model knowledge is most dangerous, because treating a convention as an obligation could reject valid 0.5 files; every obligation item must be re-verified against the specification text before implementation. Applicability and transfer limits: classification applies to OME-Zarr 0.5 as targeted by the brief only. Plan implications: the implementation plan should carry a two-column trace, obligation versus decision, per feature. Unresolved: the authoritative obligation list. Proposed validation (UNEXECUTED): line-by-line reconciliation of this classification against the OME-Zarr 0.5 specification text once an admitted copy exists.

Finding: the admitted, readable evidence base for this research goal consists of exactly two documents, TASK.md (procedural instructions, sha256 6dafd85c20e29a855ea291785bf331200df032c33e17ac2ed5ed731452c79e0c, 3061 bytes, 7 lines) and inputs/brief.md (substantive brief, sha256 f4f88faef06f7cc95c6935e2e43afe562bbdfc29ee85d984f8c59f0232c8556a, 905 bytes, 5 lines). The assignment, the thin plan, and the source corpus could not be read: workspace-root assignment.md and plan.md exist as entries but every bounded read and mechanical operation on them is rejected as out of the allowed boundary, and the directories inputs/plan and inputs/sources exist while no readable file inside them could be located across the probe census recorded in acquisition A004 and A005. Governing conditions: the bounded tool set provides no directory listing, so discovery required name probing; read tools report only FileNotFoundError, NotADirectoryError, or ValueError. Qualifications and counterevidence: per the governing task rules, these failed reads are NOT evidence that no assignment, plan, or corpus exists, and no claim of corpus-wide absence is made; correspondingly, every substantive statement in R002 through R011 that goes beyond the brief's literal text is labeled model knowledge or analysis and is not corpus-backed. Applicability and transfer limits: all findings are conditioned on this restricted evidence base and must be re-derived if further sources are admitted. Plan implications: the plan itself could not be consulted, so plan implications recorded here are inferences from the brief, not reconciliations with an actual plan. Unresolved: the content of the assignment, thin plan, and corpus. Proposed validation (UNEXECUTED): re-run acquisition with the same probe census if the boundary or corpus is amended, and reconcile any newly readable source against R001 through R011.
